correctness.rationale: For a finite theory using raw nouns \(p_1,\ldots,p_r\), the \(2^r\) Boolean membership atoms partition every finite model. Assigning a nonnegative integer count \(z_\varepsilon\) to each atom makes every Boolean noun cardinality a \(0/1\)-linear form. Inclusion, nonempty intersection, weak cardinal comparison and strict cardinal comparison become Presburger equalities/inequalities, and existentially projecting the atom counts while retaining \(N=\sum z_\varepsilon\) gives an effective Presburger definition of the finite spectrum. Replicating every element \(m\) times preserves every atomic truth value, including strict comparisons, so spectra are dilation-closed. The displayed \(k\)-block theory really partitions the universe into \(k\) pairwise-disjoint equal blocks, yielding exactly \(\{kn:n\ge1\}\). Jiang's complete primary PDF was inspected at Section 5.1 and independently confirms the same construction for \(k=3\).
risks: Presburger quantifier elimination is effective but may be computationally expensive; no complexity bound beyond effectiveness is asserted.

Thus both the upper-envelope theorem and the showcased family are mechanically implied by established frameworks/results.
